question.problem: Given that ${11}^{2x-3}=\sqrt[3]{{7}^{2}},$  find the value of $x$ rounded to $3$ decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
Taking ${log}_{11}$ of both sides of the equation gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{11}^{2x-3} & =\sqrt[3]{{7}^{2}} \\ {log}_{11}⁡({11}^{2x-3}) & ={log}_{11}⁡(\sqrt[3]{{7}^{2}}) \\ 2x-3 & ={log}_{11}⁡({7}^{2/3})\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we apply the power rule to the right-hand side:

$$
2x-3=\frac{2}{3}{log}_{11}⁡(7)
$$

Next, we rewrite the right-hand side using the change of base formula and then solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}2x-3 & =\frac{2\operatorname{log}⁡(7)}{3\operatorname{log}⁡(11)} \\ 2x & =\frac{2\operatorname{log}⁡(7)}{3\operatorname{log}⁡(11)}+3 \\ x & =\frac{\operatorname{log}⁡(7)}{3\operatorname{log}⁡(11)}+\frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluating the above on a calculator gives

$$
x≈1.771
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.
